audit.title: Data Streams Reference

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. The page opens with a title, a component placeholder (`<DataStreams section="dsNotes" />`), then link lists — no self-contained sentence answers "what is the Data Streams API / which interface do I use."

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong for its size — clear category headings (`API Interfaces`, `SDK Integration`, `Authentication`, `Verification`) and grouped bullets. Docked for the H1→H3 level skip (no H2; measured "1 level skip") which muddies chunk hierarchy.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Very weak. Measured 0 numerals, 0 units, 0 versions. No latency, update-frequency, supported-chain counts, or rate limits — exactly the specifics engines lift.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 14 internal links, 0 external. Appropriate as a hub, but no links to primary specs/standards; link labels are descriptive, which helps.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Weak. No one-to-two-sentence definition of "Data Streams" or of each interface anywhere on the page.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured: no JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no head metadata captured. The `llms.txt` pointer is a positive site-level signal.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code present. Acceptable for a pure index, but a minimal "when to use each" cue would still help; scored low as the rubric measures it.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Moderate. Covers the lifecycle surfaces (interfaces → SDK → auth → verification across EVM/Solana/Stellar) but only as link labels; no "how do I…" or "which should I choose" phrasing.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent product naming (REST API, WebSocket, Go SDK, Rust SDK). No action needed beyond the additions below.

audit.summary: This is a thin routing/index page (137 words, 14 internal links, no prose body) whose sole job is to fan out to the Data Streams API interfaces, SDKs, authentication, and verification pages. Its structural clarity is its one strength — cleanly categorized bullets under sensible headings. Its dominant GEO weakness is that it is **all links and no liftable content**: no canonical definition of the Data Streams API, no comparison of REST vs WebSocket vs SDK, no numbers, no metadata. As served it will rarely be cited by a generative engine because there is nothing quotable to lift; engines will bypass it for the child pages or answer from priors. Honest verdict: functional for humans, near-invisible for generative retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add an interface-selection comparison table
recommendations.where: new section after `### API Interfaces`, before the SDK list.
recommendations.issue: interfaces are listed as bare links: "REST API — HTTP-based interface for simple integrations."
recommendations.change: add a table with columns *Interface | Best for | Delivery model | Latency profile | Auth required*, one row each for REST, WebSocket, Go SDK, Rust SDK, with concrete values (e.g. push vs pull, sub-second streaming vs request/response).
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract *reasons* and answer "which Data Streams interface should I use," a high-intent query this page currently can't win.

recommendations.title: Lead with a canonical definition of the Data Streams API
recommendations.where: immediately under the H1, replacing/augmenting the `dsNotes` component.
recommendations.issue: page opens with no prose; first content is a component placeholder.
recommendations.change: add one to two liftable sentences: "The Chainlink Data Streams API delivers high-frequency, low-latency market data reports that are cryptographically signed and verifiable onchain. Access it via REST, WebSocket, or the Go/Rust SDKs."
recommendations.why: gives engines a self-contained, verbatim-liftable statement; defends against parametric priors when the page is only skimmed.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased subheadings
recommendations.change: add or rephrase to question form, e.g. "Which Data Streams interface should I use?", "How do I authenticate with the Data Streams API?", "How do I verify Data Streams reports onchain?"
recommendations.why: developers and agents query by task/question; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to each entry
recommendations.issue: measured 0 numerals; descriptions are purely qualitative.
recommendations.change: cite update frequency, supported networks count, SDK language versions, and rate limits where known (or link to the page that states them).
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Fix heading hierarchy (H1→H2)
recommendations.issue: measured "1 level skip"; top categories are H3 under an H1 with no H2.
recommendations.change: promote the four category headings to H2, keep `#### EVM chains`/`#### Solana` as H3.
recommendations.why: clean hierarchy improves RAG chunk boundaries and section retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata / JSON-LD
recommendations.issue: measured no JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle`/`CollectionPage` JSON-LD, a canonical URL, and a visible last-updated date. (Note: CLI did not capture `<head>` — pass raw head for full verification.)
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent trust and parseability (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Add a short chain-support summary for Verification
recommendations.issue: verification is split by chain with bare links only.
recommendations.change: one sentence naming supported chains (EVM, Solana, Stellar) and the onchain vs offchain choice, before the links.
recommendations.why: captures "does Data Streams support verification on Solana/Stellar" queries with a liftable answer.

antiPatterns: Content thinness: 137 words of almost entirely link labels — a wall of navigation with no extractable substance.
Unresolved component placeholder in served content (`<DataStreams section="dsNotes" />`) — if this fails to render, the page's only prose is lost to crawlers.
Missing dates/version signals — undated content lowers freshness trust.
offPageNotes: The `llms.txt` pointer is present and positive — a good site-level discoverability signal.
Canonical URL, JSON-LD, and sitemap coverage are template/site-level concerns; verify they are emitted site-wide, not just here.
As a hub page, its citation value depends heavily on child pages carrying the concrete answers; ensure those pages link back to this index (canonical-hub pattern).
